topic: Microsoft Clarity adds AI agent simulation assessments (agents from Google, OpenAI, Anthropic tested on tasks like checkout); weekly agent sessions ~2M, nearly doubled in 3 weeks (PPC Land, 5 Nov 2026)
instagram_caption:
Microsoft can now test if AI agents can use your website.

On 4 November, Microsoft added simulation assessments to Clarity, its website analytics tool. It sends AI agents from Google, OpenAI and Anthropic through key tasks, starting with shopping and travel journeys like checkout, and reports whether they finished, how long it took and where they got stuck. Clarity says weekly AI agent sessions on the sites it tracks nearly doubled in three weeks, to almost 2 million.

Why it matters: more shoppers will send an assistant to compare, book or buy for them. If that assistant gets stuck on a pop-up or a fiddly size selector, you may lose the sale without ever seeing it.

What to do this week:
1. Install Clarity (the analytics service is free) and check its Agent Activity dashboard to see which agents already visit you.
2. Run a simulation on your most important task, such as checkout or booking, and fix the first blocker it finds.
3. Track agent visits separately from human traffic where you can, so they don't distort your conversion rates.

Good UX now has to work for people and for the agents they send.

On 4 November, Microsoft added simulation assessments to Clarity, its website analytics tool. Clarity sends AI agents from Google, OpenAI and Anthropic through key tasks on your site, starting with commerce and travel journeys such as checkout, and reports whether each task was completed, how long it took and where the experience broke down. Clarity also reports that weekly AI agent sessions across the sites it tracks nearly doubled in three weeks, to almost 2 million.

Our view: a growing share of shoppers will send an assistant to compare, book or buy on their behalf. If that assistant gets stuck on a pop-up or a login wall, the sale may be lost without anyone on your team noticing.

Three steps worth taking this week:
1. Install Clarity, whose core analytics service is free, and check the Agent Activity dashboard to see which agents already visit your site.
2. Run a simulation on your most important task, such as checkout or booking, and fix the first blocker it finds.
3. Track agent visits separately from human traffic where possible, so they do not distort your conversion rates.

Good UX now has to work for people and for the agents they send.
